assignment: A source-isolated participant joins a legally replayed developer checkpoint. Evaluate only the assigned scene range through normal logical observations. Earlier actions were developer setup, not participant choices. Skim earned cards naturally and read optional material only when useful. Explain expected and observed contributions, concrete clarity or confusion, and any repeated work. This is bounded partial-context passage evaluation, not fresh full-campaign play or voluntary retention. Other vignettes within the same condition may have been seen; the other condition and source are withheld.

playerEvidence.intention: Test the returning rule against the harmful case.
playerEvidence.expected: The owed weapon makes the rule demand an action whose danger gives a counterexample; I expect a qualified or rejected definition, not a general ban on returning possessions.

playerEvidence.intention: I see the available bridge to definitions, but want to know exactly what the earlier explanation contributes.

playerEvidence.expected: The eclipse explanation supplies explicit conditions; the failed definition supplies a counterexample. Together these should give a way to challenge claims through their applicability, not through prestige.

intelligibility.explanation: The returning rule supplies a general claim and the dangerous weapon request a concrete counterexample. The earned card explicitly says the failed rule does not yet supply a replacement definition.

learning.explanation: Within this partial-context vignette, the distinction between exposing a faulty definition and completing a new one is explicit. Reading the conditions item made the later bridge from explanation to objection intelligible; this is not a retention test.

construction.explanation: The first operation changes the status of a definition through a particular case. Prestige then contributes a reason to examine choices independently of status. The final operation plausibly joins explicit conditions with a counterexample, although its result card emphasizes objections and standing rather than explaining the conditions input.

pacing.explanation: Three combinations completed the assigned goals without retracing them. Combining while the previous card remained visible queued the examined-life card, so its explanation arrived on dismissal. The duplicate optional read was my observation-filter mistake, not repeated game work.

continuity.explanation: I entered chapter 3 at a prepared checkpoint, not through earlier chapters. The eclipse conditions item was readable and reusable here, so local continuity can be explained, but long-run continuity is untested.

choice.explanation: The initial pair was the only substantive offered combination; its reverse was not another conceptual choice. After that I could choose the order of two branches, but both were needed for the goals.

playerReport.experience: Partial-context assigned scope: chapter 3 only, events 27–34 are my own play; events 1–26 were developer setup, not my play. I expected the weapon case to challenge rather than replace the justice definition, which the card confirmed. I skimmed earned cards and optionally read the carried conditions item. No source, route, other trial, or later chapter was accessed. I experienced mild sequencing confusion when an earlier card remained after my next combination; dismissal exposed the queued result.
playerReport.stoppingReason: Both assigned chapter 3 goals are complete at event 34. Stopped without advancing beyond the assigned chapter.
playerReport.nextExperiment: Test an independent player with the carried conditions item readable but without offered valid-pair hints; ask what each input contributes before the final combination and whether the result explicitly accounts for both.
